evidence: The rejected diff supplies only one process-substitution operand and cannot compare two sorted directory listings.
The rejected ps selects comm rather than the complete args field and malformed output-option bindings do not provide the requested full command lines.
Lowercase -i prompts for every file, whereas the requested one-time large-batch confirmation requires capital -I.
The rejected response turns regex-like text into glob filters, omits the search pattern, and does not express the Rust include and tests-directory exclusion globs.
The rejected -I option expects an interval value and does not use the workload separator before ./app.
The rejected response omits capital -P and therefore does not use the requested non-standard SSH port.
The rejected whence command omits -a and reports only the first resolution instead of every alias, function, builtin, and executable match.
The rejected gh pr watch invocation is not the checks --watch workflow requested for monitoring CI status.
The rejected pipeline does not use zsh's join expansion and invokes an unrelated external join command with invalid arguments.
The rejected response uses a three-second interval with no report count rather than one-second sampling for exactly three reports.
The rejected trailing install token is not part of uv python pin syntax and changes the requested pin operation.
The rejected g suffix replaces every occurrence rather than only the second occurrence on each line.
The rejected ss filter does not provide a concrete port or a valid established-state destination/source-port expression.
Without -n the rejected sed command prints every input line and prints the selected range a second time.
The rejected source lacks the required trailing slash and therefore copies the directory itself rather than only its contents.
The rejected gh api flags do not request Link-header pagination and include malformed pagination and jq option spellings.
pip show already reports Required-by; the rejected unsupported --requires option prevents the requested dependency inspection.
The rejected rsync command omits the destination server entirely and cannot perform the requested mirror.
The rejected filter lacks the leading ellipsis that includes dependents of the selected workspace package.
The rejected response conflicts follow mode with previous-container mode, omits the namespace binding, and does not address the deployment target correctly.
The rejected -l option is not part of the requested latest-run failed-log invocation and changes option parsing.
The rejected response fabricates unsupported uv run test flags instead of running pytest in the managed project environment.
The rejected -1 and -2 options require numeric field positions, not the literal value key.
The rejected response omits the byte limit and may dump the entire file instead of only the first bytes.
The rejected recursive Markdown glob neither restricts results to Downloads nor selects the single newest file with zsh's om[1] qualifiers.
The rejected response compares config.toml with itself, so it cannot compare the requested two configuration files.
The rejected final wc counts output rows produced by the first wc rather than the total number of source lines.
The rejected -j spelling does not select util-linux dmesg JSON output; the required option is --json.
The rejected response asks systemctl to link rather than enable the unit and invents an unsupported --service option.
The rejected ss invocation omits listening-state selection and does not form a valid filter for TCP port 8080.
The rejected scp command omits capital -P 2222 and therefore does not use the requested non-standard port.
The rejected ls command omits -R and therefore does not recursively list the docs tree.
The rejected ruff linter invocation uses an unsupported --rule form instead of ruff rule to explain the code.
The rejected ip brief form omits the required brief option spelling and address show subcommand.
The rejected response omits -c and therefore does not verify files against checksums listed in the checksum file.
The rejected route-get tail does not form a valid output-interface constraint and invents an interface absent from the request.
The rejected GNU-style stat -c spelling is unsupported by BSD stat on macOS and cannot report the requested permission bits.
The rejected tail invocation invents an unsupported -e option and omits the line-buffered grep stage needed to filter live errors.
The rejected lsof form does not reliably bind the TCP port selector and omits both LISTEN-state filtering and non-resolving output flags.
The rejected GNU --max-depth option is unsupported by BSD du on macOS, and the response omits size sorting.
The rejected response invents a --preview flag and does not provide a valid search pattern and replacement pair.
The rejected split command binds numeric operands incorrectly to -d and -n and does not specify the requested output suffix and prefix.
The rejected free command omits -h and therefore does not produce the requested human-readable memory values.
The rejected response runs unittest with a generic warning filter rather than making DeprecationWarning failures in the target application.
The rejected tr invocation adds unrelated squeezing, does not quote the control characters safely, and supplies a filename even though tr reads standard input.
The rejected comm command provides only one malformed filename operand and cannot compute a two-file set difference.
The rejected -t option lacks its radix argument and the response omits the minimum string length needed for the requested extraction.
The rejected response sets parallel jobs but omits the load-average bound required to avoid starting work while overloaded.
The rejected --diff mode only previews unsafe fixes and its tool-name operands are not a valid project-wide safe-fix invocation.
The rejected host operands treat MX as a positional server rather than selecting the MX query type with -t.
The rejected --signal 9 overrides the requested HUP signal, force-killing processes instead of asking them to reload.
The rejected zmv patterns do not capture the basename or reference that capture in the replacement, so they cannot preserve names while changing extensions.
The rejected -b t mode numbers all lines, while the requested non-empty-line behavior requires the default non-empty selection.
The rejected mktemp suffix and template arguments are malformed and do not safely create a temporary directory.
The rejected BSD ps output-option sequence is malformed and uses invalid field spellings instead of the macOS memory-sorted form.
The rejected response selects network sockets and misbinds link-count/state options instead of finding open files with link count below one.
The rejected response invents network filters and does not use +D on the mounted directory whose open files must be found.
The rejected response deletes both character classes and supplies a filename operand instead of translating upper to lower case from standard input.
The rejected response intermixes display options with duplicate filter operands and does not form a valid single BPF filter for the saved capture.
The rejected vmstat uses a five-second interval with no count instead of collecting exactly five samples at two-second intervals.
The rejected --tmpdir and template operands are bound incorrectly and do not form the requested safe default temporary-directory invocation.
The rejected response runs an unrelated gpg operation with malformed timeout durations instead of the five-second health check.
The rejected tail starts at line five rather than skipping one header and omits the stage limiting output to the first five data rows.
The rejected response uses unsupported level names and fabricated panic levels and omits non-pager output.
The rejected BSD date command omits -u and therefore formats the timestamp in local time rather than UTC.
The rejected attached -i.bak spelling is GNU-style and does not supply BSD sed's required separate backup-suffix argument on macOS.
The rejected -u flag adds UDP sockets even though the task explicitly requests every listening TCP socket.
